correctness.rationale: Generic powers-of-two diagonal conjugation has pairwise distinct nonzero weights on all off-diagonal matrix coordinates and weight zero on the diagonal subspace. Thus the projective fixed locus consists exactly of the diagonal projective space and \(n(n-1)\) isolated matrix units. Every off-diagonal matrix unit is nilpotent and hence belongs to every nonempty bounded-eigenvalue level. Inside the diagonal fixed component, equality patterns are indexed by set partitions. A block-count \(b\) stratum is \(\operatorname{Conf}_b(\mathbb C)/\mathbb C^*\); for \(b\ge2\), normalizing the first difference identifies it with \(\mathbb C\times\operatorname{Conf}_{b-2}(\mathbb C\setminus\{0,1\})\), whose compactly supported Euler characteristic is \((-1)^{b-2}(b-2)!\). Summing over \({n\brace b}\) partitions and applying algebraic torus localization proves the formula. The exact-layer formula is a direct additive difference. The packaged checker independently validates combinatorics, weight separation, and finite-field arrangement counts.

originality.rationale: The directly inspected archival source defines exactly the complex bounded-distinct-eigenvalue matrix varieties and their diagonal equality arrangements, then proves invariant-theoretic statements about subdiscriminants; it contains no Euler or Poincaré occurrence. Targeted semantic-database and web searches for the exact complex projective object, subdiscriminants, topology, Euler characteristic, Poincaré polynomial, and the Stirling-number form of the answer found no covering statement. Vassiliev gives finer topology for Hermitian operators filtered by eigenvalue multiplicity, but that is a different real-Hermitian parameter space and does not imply the projective complex-matrix formula. The closest previously recorded eigenvalue result compares a matrix spectrum with that of a northwest cutoff and therefore imposes a different condition.

value.rationale: The bounded-distinct-eigenvalue varieties are the natural subdiscriminant filtration of projective matrix space and are explicitly studied in archival invariant theory. The theorem gives a closed invariant for every matrix size and every filtration level, and the exact strata exhibit a clean signed Stirling law. It explains nonmonotone Euler behavior of nested singular varieties and separates a universal nilpotent fixed-point contribution \(n(n-1)\) from the configuration-space combinatorics of diagonal eigenvalues. This is an all-family structural invariant of a literature-defined algebraic filtration, not an arbitrary finite slice.
